# Introduction

**ConvergeR** is an analytical toolkit designed to compute, visualize, and
statistically evaluate the convergence of single-cell states, based on the
methodology established by
[Whitfield et al. (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1158/0008-5472.can-25-4403).

All functions work directly on a `SingleCellExperiment` object (or any
`SummarizedExperiment`) as well as on a `Seurat` object. They only read and write
the cell-level metadata (`colData()` for a `SingleCellExperiment`, `meta.data`
for a `Seurat` object): the object is never converted, and is returned with its
original class and all its content (assays, reduced dimensions, ...) untouched,
with the new score columns added to the cell metadata.

In this vignette, we demonstrate the package workflow on a subset of the PBMC3k
dataset (Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells). For each cell, we evaluate the
balance between two opposing programs from the MSigDB Hallmark collection:
the interferon alpha response versus the inflammatory response. The main
workflow uses a `SingleCellExperiment`; a short section at the end shows that
the exact same calls work on a `Seurat` object.

# 1. Environment Setup and Data Preparation

Let's load the required packages and the lightweight subset of the PBMC dataset
bundled with the package.

```{r}
library(ConvergeR)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(ggplot2)

# Load the built-in example dataset
sce_path <- system.file("extdata", "pbmc3k_subset_sce.rds", package = "ConvergeR")
sce <- readRDS(sce_path)
sce
```

To simulate a multi-patient cohort, we inject mock clinical metadata. Patient-level
covariates (age, tumor status, treatment) are constant within a patient, which is
what the patient-level tests below assume. These data are simulated, so the
results shown in this vignette have no biological meaning.

```{r}
set.seed(42)

patients <- paste0("Patient_", 1:8)
clinical <- data.frame(
  SS = patients,
  age = c(25, 33, 47, 52, 68, 41, 59, 36),
  tumor_status = rep(c("Primary", "Metastatic"), 4),
  treatment = rep(c("Treated", "Treated", "Untreated", "Untreated"), 2)
)

# Randomly assign each cell to a patient, then copy the patient's covariates
sce$SS <- sample(patients, ncol(sce), replace = TRUE)
idx <- match(sce$SS, clinical$SS)
sce$age <- clinical$age[idx]
sce$tumor_status <- clinical$tumor_status[idx]
sce$treatment <- clinical$treatment[idx]
```

# 2. Importing MSigDB Signatures and Scoring

Instead of manually importing `.gmt` files, we use the `msigdbr` package to
directly retrieve the official Hallmark signatures.

```{r}
library(msigdbr)

hallmark_sets <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "H")

raw_group1 <- hallmark_sets[hallmark_sets$gs_name == "HALLMARK_INTERFERON_ALPHA_RESPONSE", ]$gene_symbol
raw_group2 <- hallmark_sets[hallmark_sets$gs_name == "HALLMARK_INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE", ]$gene_symbol

# Keep only the genes actually present in the dataset
group1_genes <- intersect(raw_group1, rownames(sce))
group2_genes <- intersect(raw_group2, rownames(sce))
```

ConvergeR only needs one numeric score per cell and per program, stored in the cell
metadata. Any scoring method can be used (for example `AUCell`, `UCell` or
`singscore`; `AddModuleScore()` for Seurat objects). For simplicity, we use here the
mean log-normalized expression of each signature.

```{r}
sce <- scuttle::logNormCounts(sce)

sce$Score_IFN <- colMeans(as.matrix(logcounts(sce)[group1_genes, , drop = FALSE]))
sce$Score_Inflam <- colMeans(as.matrix(logcounts(sce)[group2_genes, , drop = FALSE]))
```

# 3. Computing the Convergence Score

`CalculateConvergedScore()` standardizes each score (Z-score), combines the scores
of each group, rescales them to $[0, 1]$ and returns their log2 ratio. A positive
value means that the cell converges towards the principal group, a negative value
towards the other group. Each group can be made of a single score or of several
scores (`principal_score = c("Score_A", "Score_B")`).

```{r}
sce <- CalculateConvergedScore(
  object = sce,
  principal_score = "Score_IFN",
  other_scores = "Score_Inflam",
  principal_name = "Interferon",
  other_name = "Inflammatory",
  output_colname = "Converged_Immune",
  principal_color = "#9b59b6", # Purple for Interferon
  other_color = "#e67e22"      # Orange for Inflammatory
)

head(colData(sce)[, c("Converged_Immune", "Converged_Immune_Direction")])
table(sce$Converged_Immune_Direction)
```

# 4. Visualization

ConvergeR automatically reads the color metadata generated in the previous step to
produce standardized plots.

## Proportion Barplot

Proportion of cells converging to either Immune state across our 8 mock patients.

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, fig.align='center'}
PlotConvergenceProportion(
  object = sce,
  x_var = "SS",
  fill_var = "Converged_Immune_Direction",
  title = "Immune Convergence by Patient"
)
```

## Crossed Proportion Barplot

Faceted by tumor status to identify subgroup trends.

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, fig.align='center'}
PlotConvergenceCrossedProportion(
  object = sce,
  x_var = "SS",
  fill_var = "Converged_Immune_Direction",
  facet_var = "tumor_status",
  title = "Immune Convergence split by Tumor Status"
)
```

## Density Distribution

Continuous relationship of the convergence direction with patient age.

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, fig.align='center'}
PlotConvergenceDensity(
  object = sce,
  x_var = "age",
  fill_var = "Converged_Immune_Direction",
  x_label = "Patient Age"
)
```

# 5. Statistical Testing

We evaluate the statistical significance at the patient level (pseudobulk) to
prevent pseudoreplication bias caused by single-cell testing.

## Bivariate Test

```{r}
TestConvergenceScore(
  object = sce,
  score_var = "Converged_Immune",
  test_var = "age",
  level = "patient",
  patient_id_var = "SS"
)
```

**How to read this result:** The output message displays the statistical test used
(e.g., Spearman correlation for continuous variables), the analysis level
(patient pseudobulk to avoid single-cell pseudoreplication), the number of
observations ($N$ patients), and the p-value. A p-value below 0.05 indicates a
statistically significant association between the convergence score and the
tested variable.

## Multivariate Linear Model

```{r}
TestMultivariateConvergence(
  object = sce,
  score_var = "Converged_Immune",
  test_vars = c("age", "tumor_status", "treatment"),
  level = "patient",
  patient_id_var = "SS"
)
```

**How to read this result:** This model fits a multivariable linear regression on
pseudobulk data. It details the global model performance ($R^2$ and global
p-value) and breaks down the independent effect (Estimate) and significance
(p-value accompanied by conventional significance stars) for each covariate,
allowing you to assess the effect of a variable while controlling for potential
confounders.

# 6. Working with Seurat Objects

The same functions accept a `Seurat` object, with the same arguments. Here we build
a `Seurat` object from the counts and the metadata of the `SingleCellExperiment`
used above (before the convergence score was computed).

```{r, eval = has_seurat}
seu <- SeuratObject::CreateSeuratObject(
  counts = counts(sce),
  meta.data = as.data.frame(
    colData(sce)[, c("SS", "age", "tumor_status", "treatment",
                     "Score_IFN", "Score_Inflam")]
  )
)
```

With a `Seurat` object, the module scores would typically be computed with
`Seurat::AddModuleScore()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
seu <- Seurat::NormalizeData(seu)
seu <- Seurat::AddModuleScore(seu, features = list(group1_genes), name = "Score_IFN_")
seu <- Seurat::AddModuleScore(seu, features = list(group2_genes), name = "Score_Inflam_")
seu$Score_IFN <- seu$Score_IFN_1
seu$Score_Inflam <- seu$Score_Inflam_1
```

Here we simply reuse the scores computed above so that both objects can be
compared. The convergence score is then computed, plotted and tested exactly as
for the `SingleCellExperiment`:

```{r, eval = has_seurat}
seu <- CalculateConvergedScore(
  object = seu,
  principal_score = "Score_IFN",
  other_scores = "Score_Inflam",
  principal_name = "Interferon",
  other_name = "Inflammatory",
  output_colname = "Converged_Immune",
  principal_color = "#9b59b6",
  other_color = "#e67e22"
)

class(seu)

# Same result as with the SingleCellExperiment
all.equal(unname(seu$Converged_Immune), unname(sce$Converged_Immune))
```

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, fig.align='center', eval = has_seurat}
PlotConvergenceProportion(
  object = seu,
  x_var = "SS",
  fill_var = "Converged_Immune_Direction",
  title = "Immune Convergence by Patient (Seurat object)"
)
```

```{r, eval = has_seurat}
TestConvergenceScore(
  object = seu,
  score_var = "Converged_Immune",
  test_var = "age",
  level = "patient",
  patient_id_var = "SS"
)
```
